stem:
Tara checks whether whole numbers are perfect cubes and computes simple cubes.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call $64$ a perfect cube label only, with no check that some whole number cubes to $64$.
$100$ is a perfect cube because it ends with two zeros.
$4^{3} = 64$, so $64$ is a perfect cube; also $3^{3} = 27$.
$27$ is a perfect cube even when the edge length is not a whole number of unit cubes.

teacher.key_rationale: 64=4³ and 27=3³ are perfect cubes. Naming the label alone skips the computation. Trailing zeros do not make 100 a cube. Whole-number edge length is part of the unit-cube reading.
